evidence.observation: The core barrel is the public, host-neutral surface of MemoryCore. Lines 31-34 re-export `InstanceConfigProvider` (and `LocalConfigSource`) from `./instance-config-provider.js`, which is what makes the provider's cache-gated `resolveVdb` operation part of the recorded core contract. Because the provider takes its upstream `IConfigSource` by dependency injection, this exported symbol is the exact seam a fake client can be substituted into without touching production code.

This private method is where the success state is committed. It first `await`s the client effect at line 216 (`await this.source.fetchVdb(instanceId)`), rejects an unusable payload at lines 219-223, and only then writes the cache entry with `this.vdbPool.set(...)` at lines 231-235. A rejecting client fetch propagates out of the method, so no cache entry is ever written for a failed operation — the ordering of await-before-set is the commit gate under test.

The public entry point of the operation. It returns an existing cache entry only when one is already present and unexpired (lines 181-190), dedupes concurrent first access onto a single in-flight client promise via `vdbFetchPromises` (lines 193-197), and deletes that in-flight marker in a `finally` block (lines 204-208) so a rejected fetch cannot strand the instance. Together with `fetchAndStoreVdb` this is what the fake-client test drives and observes through the public `poolSize` accessor.

The fake client used by the test. It implements the real `IConfigSource` contract but its `fetchVdb` never settles on its own — it parks a {resolve, reject} pair that the test later drives through `completeEffect()` / `failEffect()`. This is what turns 'before the client effect completes' into an observable instant instead of a race, and what lets the test assert both halves of the contract: no success state committed pre-effect, and failure observably propagated.

The five executable contract cases, all against the real provider: (1) no cache entry while the effect is pending, with poolSize re-asserted after a microtask drain so a premature `set()` would be caught; (2) concurrent callers share one effect and commit once, after it completes; (3) a failing effect rejects and caches nothing; (4) after a failure a retry reaches the client again (no stranded in-flight marker) and can then commit; (5) an unusable payload surfaces as an observable failure with no cached state. A companion case at lines 204-210 asserts the barrel in `src/core/index.ts` really re-exports `InstanceConfigProvider`.

claims.claim: The operation under contract is public MemoryCore API: `InstanceConfigProvider` is re-exported from the core barrel `MemoryCore/src/core/index.ts` (lines 31-34), and it receives its client (`IConfigSource`) by constructor injection, so a fake client can exercise the real production object.

No success state is committed before the fake effect completes: `resolveVdb` only serves cache hits for entries that already exist, and `fetchAndStoreVdb` awaits `source.fetchVdb()` before it writes `vdbPool`, so `poolSize` remains 0 for the entire window in which the fake client's fetch promise is pending.

Failure remains observable: a rejecting client fetch propagates out of `resolveVdb` (nothing is swallowed into a cached success), no cache entry is written for the failed instance, and the in-flight dedupe marker is cleared in a `finally` block so a subsequent retry re-issues the client operation instead of awaiting a permanently rejected promise.

The delivered test proves the contract executably: it drives the real `InstanceConfigProvider` through a manually-settled fake `IConfigSource` and asserts poolSize stays 0 until the effect settles, that rejection surfaces to the caller, that the failed instance is not stranded, and that the barrel exposes the symbol under test.

conclusion: MemoryCore's exported `InstanceConfigProvider` satisfies the requested contract. Driven by a fake `IConfigSource` client whose operation only settles when the test says so, the real provider commits no success state (no VDB cache entry; `poolSize` stays 0) while the client effect is pending, commits exactly once after the effect resolves, and keeps failure observable: a rejected effect propagates to the caller, leaves no cached state, and clears its in-flight dedupe marker so a retry can still succeed. A negative control confirmed the gating assertion is not vacuous — a mutant that writes the cache entry before awaiting the client fetch is caught by the same assertion.
